landing.title: Saylov-Media: transforming political journalism
landing.subtitle: A platform for the comprehensive assessment, monitoring and comparative analysis of digital media covering electoral processes, across seven criteria.

model.title: The seven criteria of the MS-7 model
model.subtitle: Each criterion measures a distinct aspect of a digital outlet's work. Together they form a single composite indicator.

scale.title: The SMSI assessment scale
scale.subtitle: The index is interpreted on a 100-point scale and supports evidence-based management decisions.

cta.title: See the system in action
cta.subtitle: Enter scores across the seven criteria — the composite index and radar chart recalculate in real time.

formula.title: How the SMSI index adds up
formula.subtitle: Scroll — each criterion contributes its weighted share while the radar builds vertex by vertex.

calculator.indexSubtitleEqual: Saylov Media Samaradorligi Indexi · with equal weights

selected.label: Selected outlet

save.failed: Could not save. Check the connection and your permissions.

calculator.scaleSubtitle: The SMSI index is interpreted on a 100-point scale.

mode.directHint: Each criterion receives a single score.
mode.indicatorsHint: Score the indicators; each criterion is their average, rounded to a whole number. Indicators are saved with the assessment, so the result can be audited.

rating.title: Digital media effectiveness ranking
rating.subtitle: A comparative ranking of outlets assessed with the MS-7 model, based on the SMSI composite index.
rating.demoNotice: The scores below were generated to showcase the interface and are not the result of real monitoring. Once Supabase is connected, the ranking is read from the media_rankings table.

filters.shareHint: The filter is kept in the page address, so the link can be shared.

empty.title: No outlets in this slice
empty.text: Pick another ownership type or region.

rating.smallSample: Small sample: {count, plural, one {# outlet} other {# outlets}}. The average is unstable — compare with caution.

compare.title: State-owned vs private outlets
compare.subtitle: Group averages: the SMSI index and the seven criteria.
compare.diffNote: Difference is private minus state-owned. A positive value means private outlets score higher.
compare.emptyGroup: One of the groups has no outlets, so they cannot be compared.

regions.title: Regional ranking
regions.subtitle: Average SMSI of outlets in each region.
regions.single: All assessed outlets are from one region so far. A regional comparison will appear once other regions have data.
regions.smallNote: * — fewer than three outlets: the average is unstable.

agreement.title: Expert agreement in this round
agreement.subtitle: Kendall's coefficient of concordance W over the outlets rated by every expert in the round: 0 means no agreement, 1 means the experts rank the outlets identically.
agreement.significant: Agreement is statistically significant (p < 0.05): the experts' rankings are not random.
agreement.notSignificant: Agreement is not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.05): matching ranks may be due to chance.
agreement.single: Only one expert rated this round, so agreement is not calculated.
agreement.noCommon: Fewer than two outlets were rated by every expert in the round, so W is not calculated. Use the per-outlet spread instead.
agreement.flagged: {count, plural, =0 {No outlets need consensus.} one {# outlet needs consensus: the SMSI range between experts exceeds 5 points.} other {# outlets need consensus: the SMSI range between experts exceeds 5 points.}}
agreement.scale: Scale: below 0.2 very weak, 0.2–0.4 weak, 0.4–0.6 moderate, 0.6–0.8 strong, 0.8 and above very strong.

methodology.title: The MS-7 assessment model and the SMSI composite index
methodology.subtitle: MS-7 (Media Saylov — 7 mezonli baholash) is a model for the comprehensive assessment of how digital media cover electoral processes. Each criterion carries a weighting coefficient, and the result is expressed as a single figure — the SMSI index.
methodology.algorithmSubtitle: The composite index is the weighted sum of the criterion scores.
methodology.formulaNote: Each criterion is scored from 0 to 100, so the index also falls between 0 and 100. Legal compliance and information quality carry the greatest weight: during an election they determine the legality and reliability of the information flow.
methodology.scaleSubtitle: The scale supports interpretation of results and management decisions.

weights.title: Weight versions
weights.subtitle: Each assessment's index is fixed when it is saved, using the weight set in force on the assessment date. A new weight version does not recalculate past rounds.
weights.builtin: Weights are shown from the application code: the database is not connected or migration 006 has not been run.
weights.mismatchTitle: Interface weights differ from the database.
weights.mismatch: The calculator uses the weights in code (version {ui}), while new assessments are saved with version {db} from the database. Update lib/ms7.ts.

legal.name: Legal compliance
legal.description: How closely the outlet follows current legislation and journalistic ethics when covering elections.
indicators: Equal treatment of all political actors

quality.name: Information quality
quality.description: The substance, completeness and reliability of the information published.

speed.name: Operational efficiency
speed.description: The ability to deliver information about electoral events promptly and on time.

multimedia.name: Multimedia integration
multimedia.description: How well information is presented across formats — text, visual and audio.

interactivity.name: Audience interaction
interactivity.description: The breadth of opportunities for dialogue and exchange with the audience.

engagement.name: Audience engagement
engagement.description: How the audience receives digital content and how widely it spreads.

convergence.name: Media convergence
convergence.description: Simultaneous distribution across digital platforms and a cross-platform approach.

veryhigh.label: Very high
veryhigh.interpretation: The media system fully meets international standards, is stable and innovatively developed.

high.label: High
high.interpretation: A stable system is in place; certain areas still require improvement.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.interpretation: Core institutions function, but the system has weak points.

poor.label: Unsatisfactory
poor.interpretation: Stability is low; legal and economic problems are pronounced.

critical.label: Critical
critical.interpretation: The media system has systemic problems; institutional and economic reform is required.

outlet.rounds: {count, plural, one {# monitoring round} other {# monitoring rounds}}
outlet.dynamicsSubtitle: How the composite index changes across monitoring rounds.
outlet.needMore: A trend needs at least two rounds. This outlet has a single assessment so far.
outlet.profileSubtitle: Current round compared with the previous one.

consensus.title: Expert agreement
consensus.subtitle: Round scores are the mean of the experts' scores; SMSI is calculated from the means. Individual scores are not published.
consensus.flagText: The SMSI range between experts exceeds 5 points, so the scores should be discussed and reconciled.
consensus.ok: The experts' scores agree: the SMSI range is 5 points or less.
consensus.single: Only one expert rated this outlet in this round, so there is no spread.

recommendations.title: Recommendations
recommendations.subtitle: Derived from scores and weights by a deterministic rule — every figure can be recalculated.
recommendations.top: The outlet is at the top of the scale. Below is where headroom remains.
recommendations.pathTitle: Shortest path to the next level
recommendations.pathBroad: One or two criteria are not enough: {count} of 7 criteria must reach {target}. The profile is even — broad improvement is required.
recommendations.rule: Priority = weight × headroom to 100. The path is the fewest criteria that close the gap.

report.title: Media performance assessment report
report.hint: The document is laid out for A4. To get a file, choose “Save as PDF” in the print dialog.
report.contributionNote: Contribution = score × weight. The index was recorded by the database when the assessment was saved; the sum of rounded contributions may differ from it by 0.1.
report.path: Shortest path to the next level:
report.footer: Generated by the MS-7: Saylov-Media platform. The report number combines the outlet's database ID and the assessment date, so the document can be matched against the database.
report.demo: Demo data: this report was generated to demonstrate the interface and is not a monitoring result.
report.periodMissing: Round “{period}” was not found for this outlet, so the latest round is shown.
